questions.question: Which of the following was enacted in 1860 in British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Indian Penal Code**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** was enacted in 1860.
 
• The IPC is the comprehensive code intended to cover all substantive aspects of criminal law in India.
 
• It was drafted by the first law commission under the chairmanship of **Lord Macaulay**.
 
• The IPC has been amended several times to incorporate new laws and regulations.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Option 1: The Permanent Settlement of Bengal
 Introduced in 1793 by Lord Cornwallis, it was an agreement between the East India Company and Bengali landlords to fix revenues.
 
 

 Option 2: Hindu Widow's Remarriage Act
 Enacted in 1856, it legalized the remarriage of Hindu widows in British India.
 
 

 Option 3: Indian Penal Code
 Enacted in 1860, it is the main criminal code of India, covering all substantive aspects of criminal law.
 
 

 Option 4: Indian Evidence Act
 Enacted in 1872, it sets the rules and procedures regarding admissibility of evidence in Indian courts.

questions.question: Who has been awarded the title 'Governor of the Year' for 2023 by Central Banking, an international economic research journal?

Shaktikanta Das has been awarded the title 'Governor of the Year' for 2023 by Central Banking. Central Banking is an international economic research journal. The award recognizes Shaktikanta Das's leadership and contributions to the Indian economy. Shaktikanta Das is the current Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).  Central Banking
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Definition
 Central Banking refers to the management of a country's currency, money supply, and interest rates by its central bank.
 
 

 Functions
 The primary functions include monetary policy implementation, financial stability, and regulation of financial institutions.
 
 

 Examples
 Major central banks include the Federal Reserve (USA), European Central Bank (EU), and the Reserve Bank of India (India).
 
 

 Importance
 Central banks play a critical role in managing economic stability, controlling inflation, and stimulating economic growth.

questions.question: Which cellular structure controls cell motility, adhesion, and polarity at interphase, and facilitates the organisation of spindle poles during mitosis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Centrosomes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Centrosomes** are critical for the organization of microtubules in the cell.
 
• They play a significant role in controlling cell motility, adhesion, and polarity during interphase.
 
• During mitosis, centrosomes help in the organization of spindle poles, ensuring proper chromosome segregation.
 
• Centrosomes consist of two centrioles surrounded by an amorphous mass of protein known as the pericentriolar material.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Option 1
 **Centrosomes:** Involved in microtubule organization and spindle pole formation during mitosis.
 
 

 Option 2
 **Peroxisomes:** Organelles that contain enzymes for oxidative reactions, particularly in lipid metabolism.
 
 

 Option 3
 **Lysosomes:** Contain digestive enzymes to break down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
 

 Option 4
 **Glyoxysomes:** Specialized peroxisomes found in plants, involved in converting fat into sugar.

questions.question: Which chemical compound is present in hard plastic such as drinking water bottles and many household items?

questions.question: In 1850, Kashmir was sold under which of the following treaties to the Dogra dynasty of Jammu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Treaty of Amritsar**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kashmir** was sold to the Dogra dynasty of Jammu under the **Treaty of Amritsar** in 1846.
 
• The treaty was signed between the British East India Company and **Maharaja Gulab Singh** of Jammu.
 
• The British sold Kashmir for a sum of **7.5 million Nanakshahee rupees**.
 
• The treaty effectively established the **Dogra rule** over the region of Jammu and Kashmir.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Key Aspect
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Treaty of Amritsar**
 The treaty signed in 1846 that transferred the territories of Jammu and Kashmir to Maharaja Gulab Singh.
 
 

 **Maharaja Gulab Singh**
 The founder of the Dogra dynasty and the first Maharaja of the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
 

 **Dogra Dynasty**
 A Rajput dynasty that ruled Jammu and Kashmir from 1846 to 1947.
 
 

 **Nanakshahee Rupees**
 The currency used during the time of the Sikh Empire and later by the Dogra rulers.

questions.question: Potato chips manufacturers usually flush bags of chips with gas such as nitrogen primarily to:

options.text: make the packets look bigger for commercial advantages
prevent the chips from getting broken during transport
prevent the chips from getting oxidised
prevent decomposition of the chips by bacteria action

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **prevent the chips from getting oxidised**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxidation Prevention:** Nitrogen is an inert gas that prevents oxygen in the air from reacting with the potato chips.
 
• **Maintains Freshness:** By preventing oxidation, nitrogen helps maintain the chips' freshness and flavor for a longer time.
 
• **Extended Shelf Life:** The absence of oxygen reduces the rate of spoilage, thereby extending the product's shelf life.
 
• **Avoids Rancidity:** Oxidation can cause the oils in the chips to become rancid, and nitrogen flushing helps avoid this.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Option 1
 Making the packets look bigger is a marketing strategy but not the primary reason for using nitrogen.
 
 

 Option 2
 Preventing chips from breaking is a secondary benefit, but not the main purpose of nitrogen flushing.
 
 

 Option 3
 The correct answer: Nitrogen prevents oxidation, which is the primary reason for its use.
 
 

 Option 4
 While nitrogen can reduce bacterial growth, it is not the primary reason for its use in chip bags.

questions.question: The first Governor of RBI was ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Sir Osborne Smith**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Osborne Smith** was the first Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
• He served as the Governor from **April 1, 1935**, to **June 30, 1937**.
 
• Sir Osborne Smith was a professional banker and had previously worked with the **Bank of New South Wales**.
 
• He was appointed as the RBI Governor during the British rule in India.
 
• His tenure was marked by the initial establishment and organization of the RBI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Role
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Governor
 The highest-ranking official in the Reserve Bank of India, responsible for overseeing the bank's functions.
 
 

 Deputy Governor
 An official who assists the Governor in the management of the RBI, usually there are multiple Deputy Governors.
 
 

 Monetary Policy
 Policies formulated by the RBI to control the supply of money, often targeting inflation or interest rates.
 
 

 Banking Regulation
 The process by which the RBI oversees and regulates banks to ensure financial stability.
 
 

 Currency Issuance
 The RBI is responsible for the issuance and supply of the Indian currency notes and coins.
 
 

 Financial Inclusion
 Efforts made by the RBI to ensure that all sections of society have access to financial services.

 The RBI manages the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) and oversees foreign exchange transactions in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is an invisible biological hazard in food?
questions.solution:

• **Molds** are a type of fungi that can grow on food and are invisible to the naked eye until they form colonies.
 
• They produce spores that can contaminate food and potentially cause health issues if ingested.
 
• Molds can produce mycotoxins, which are toxic substances that can lead to foodborne illnesses.
 
• Unlike visible biological hazards like worms or weevils, molds are often not detected until they have significantly grown.

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Molds
 Molds are microscopic fungi that can grow on food, producing spores and mycotoxins, which can cause health issues.
 
 

 Worms
 Worms are visible parasites that can contaminate food but are not invisible hazards.
 
 

 Weevils
 Weevils are small beetles that infest grains and seeds, but they are visible to the naked eye.
 
 

 Fly
 Flies are insects that can contaminate food through physical contact, but they are visible.

 Position
 Description

questions.question: Which of the following is the oldest dated fort in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Kangra Fort**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kangra Fort** is considered the oldest dated fort in India, with references dating back to the Mahabharata period.
 
• The fort is located in the Kangra Valley, in the state of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• It was built by the Katoch dynasty, one of the oldest surviving dynasties in the world.
 
• The fort has witnessed numerous invasions, including those by Mahmud of Ghazni and the Mughal emperor Jahangir.
 
• Kangra Fort is renowned for its architectural grandeur and historical significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Feature
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Location**
 The fort is situated in the Kangra Valley, Himachal Pradesh.
 
 

 **Dynasty**
 The Katoch dynasty, one of the oldest royal dynasties in the world.
 
 

 **Historical Significance**
 The fort has been a witness to numerous historical events and invasions.
 
 

 **Architecture**
 Renowned for its architectural grandeur and strategic construction.
 
 

 **Invasions**
 Invaded by Mahmud of Ghazni and Mughal emperor Jahangir, among others.

questions.question: The maximum limit on microfinance loans for NBFCs other than NBFC-MFIs is _________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **25% of the total assets**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The maximum limit on microfinance loans for NBFCs other than NBFC-MFIs is 25% of the total assets.
 
• This regulation ensures that NBFCs diversify their loan portfolios and do not overly expose themselves to microfinance loans.
 
• NBFCs (Non-Banking Financial Companies) are financial institutions that offer various banking services but do not have a banking license.
 
• **Microfinance loans are small loans provided to individuals or small businesses who do not have access to traditional banking services.
 
• NBFC-MFIs are a specific category of NBFCs that primarily deal with microfinance activities and have different regulatory requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Microfinance** is a type of financial service aimed at providing small loans, savings, and other financial services to **low-income individuals** or those who do not have access to traditional banking services. It plays a crucial role in **financial inclusion** and economic development by empowering individuals to start or expand small businesses, improve their living standards, and achieve financial stability.

 
 

 Term
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Microfinance
 Financial services provided to low-income individuals or groups who are typically excluded from traditional banking services.
 
 

 NBFC
 Non-Banking Financial Companies that offer various financial services but do not hold a banking license.
 
 

 NBFC-MFI
 A specific category of NBFCs that primarily deal with microfinance activities.
 
 

 Financial Inclusion
 The effort to make financial services accessible to all individuals, especially those who are underserved by traditional financial institutions.
 
 

 Loan Portfolio Diversification
 The practice of spreading loan investments across various sectors to reduce risk.

questions.question: A concave spherical mirror has radius of curvature of 30 cm. An object was placed 15 cm away of the pole in front of the mirror on the principal axis. Choose the correct option for the position, size and nature of the image formed, respectively.

options.text: Behind the mirror, enlarged, virtual and erect
At infinity, highly enlarged, real and inverted
Between Focus and Centre, diminished, real and inverted
At the focus, highly diminished point-sized, real and inverted

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **At infinity, highly enlarged, real and inverted**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror:** The given mirror is a concave spherical mirror.
 
• **Radius of Curvature:** The radius of curvature is 30 cm, so the focal length (f) = R/2 = 15 cm.
 
• **Object Position:** The object is placed 15 cm from the pole, which means it is at the focal point of the mirror.
 
• **Image Nature:** When an object is at the focal point of a concave mirror, the image formed is at infinity, highly enlarged, real, and inverted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Mirror Type
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Concave Mirror**
 A mirror with a surface that curves inward, like the inside of a bowl.
 
 

 **Convex Mirror**
 A mirror with a surface that curves outward, like the outside of a sphere.
 
 

 **Plane Mirror**
 A flat mirror that reflects light to form an upright virtual image the same size as the object.
 
 

 **Focal Point**
 The point where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to diverge after reflecting from the mirror.
 
 

 **Radius of Curvature**
 The distance between the center of curvature and the mirror's surface.
